changes.before: Implement findNote(notes,id). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Find a note by its ID, regardless of its position in the list.

before: An identity is not an array position. Deletions and reordering can make the second array element have an ID other than two.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
find calls its predicate on records until one matches. === compares the stored ID with the requested ID. ?? converts the missing result, undefined, into this API’s null marker.

Read the function call findNote([{"id":4,"title":"Moon"},{"id":9,"title":"Sea"}], 9) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, findNote runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
A note has ID 9 but is the first item. Which lookup is correct? Identity lookup searches the ID field. Its current position is incidental.
after: An ID identifies a record. An array position tells you where a record sits now. Moving or deleting items can change positions without changing their IDs.
find checks items until one passes its test. note => note.id === id asks whether the current note has the requested ID. Exact comparison keeps a numeric ID separate from text that looks the same.
find returns undefined when no note matches. ?? null replaces that missing result with null, which this function uses to mean not found.
The function returns the matching note object. It does not create a copy of that object or change the array. Keep it unchanged during this lookup.
Complete findNote(notes, id). Return the first note whose id matches exactly, or null when none does. Do not use the requested ID as an array position.
